brief: Morgan Stanley argues the market's reaction to the US midterm election results is overdone. The new data center review process pushes about 20% of US projects, roughly 5GW, from 2028 to 2029, not a reduction, because newly elected Texas and Ohio governors are unlikely to disrupt construction already under way. Aggregate hyperscaler capex stays unchanged at $1.6T/$1.8T in 2027/2028, with Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft and Oracle capex forecasts individually reaffirmed. The delay elongates the capex cycle, improving the credit outlook and lease rates and favoring the largest, best-capitalized players. The Powering AI model still shows a powered data center shortfall above 30% through 2028. Semis multiples have compressed to attractive levels, with Nvidia and Broadcom near 9x CY28 P/E, and the firm prefers compute over memory, analog and networking. AI-related debt issuance has reached $543bn, more than double FY25's level, with hyperscalers the largest issuers and a widening quality divide between issuers. Morgan Stanley recommends buying the drop across hyperscalers, select data-center supply chain names and software enablers/AI adopters, arguing S&P 500 earnings exposure to the capex pushout is limited.
